reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Most common monogenic cause of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, presenting with persistent oral, oesophageal, cutaneous and nail Candida infection often from early childhood
The paradox is that a gain-of-function variant produces immunodeficiency by suppressing the T-helper-17 responses needed for mucosal antifungal defence
A broad accompanying phenotype includes autoimmunity such as thyroid disease and type 1 diabetes, autoimmune cytopenias and enteropathy
Cerebral and systemic aneurysms and vascular disease are recognised and can cause catastrophic events
There is an increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma, particularly oral and oesophageal, arising in chronically inflamed candidal mucosa
Susceptibility extends to viral, mycobacterial and invasive fungal infection beyond Candida in more severe cases
Inheritance is autosomal dominant, usually from heterozygous variants in the coiled-coil or DNA-binding domains of STAT1
Targeted therapy with a JAK inhibitor can dampen the excessive STAT1 signalling and improve refractory disease, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is considered in severe cases
reference.pathophysiology: STAT1 is a signal transducer activated downstream of type I, type II and type III interferons and of interleukin-27. Gain-of-function variants impair the normal dephosphorylation of STAT1, leaving it persistently phosphorylated and producing exaggerated interferon-driven gene expression. This heightened STAT1 activity suppresses the differentiation of interleukin-17-producing T-helper-17 cells, which are essential for mucosal defence against Candida, explaining the chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. The same interferon over-activity fosters loss of immune tolerance with autoimmunity, contributes to vascular pathology and, together with chronic mucosal inflammation, raises the risk of squamous malignancy.
additionalDifferentials: Acquired immunosuppression or endocrinopathy causing candidiasis
additionalInvestigations: Flow-cytometric assay of STAT1 phosphorylation and dephosphorylation kinetics after interferon stimulation
Serum immunoglobulins and autoantibody screen including thyroid and endocrine autoantibodies
Full blood count for autoimmune cytopenias
STAT1 gene sequencing for gain-of-function variants
Vascular imaging where aneurysm or cerebrovascular disease is suspected
redFlags: New oral or oesophageal lesion suggesting squamous cell carcinoma in chronically infected mucosa
Neurological symptoms or headache raising concern for cerebral aneurysm
Invasive or disseminated fungal, mycobacterial or viral infection
Severe autoimmune cytopenia or refractory enteropathy
reference.prognosis: The course ranges from relatively mild mucocutaneous disease to severe multisystem involvement; life-limiting complications include invasive infection, squamous malignancy and vascular events, though targeted JAK inhibition has improved outcomes in refractory cases.
pitfalls: Treating recurrent candidiasis symptomatically without recognising an underlying inborn error
Assuming a gain-of-function variant cannot cause infection susceptibility
Overlooking associated autoimmunity, vascular disease and malignancy risk
Failing to distinguish it from APECED, which requires different surveillance
Starting broad immunosuppression that may worsen infection without considering targeted therapy
